message.content: This codebase uses lowercase comments with square-bracket annotations to maintain a consistent, machine-readable annotation format that separates semantic intent from implementation detail. The lowercase convention prevents comment noise from interfering with code folding, search indexing, and diff readability, while the square-bracket syntax — like `[intent: ...]` or `[variant: ...]` — provides a structured, parsable metadata layer that tools can consume without parsing natural language. This style also signals that annotations are part of the code’s type system rather than prose, making them stable across refactors and giving linters a clear contract for what each comment represents.
